why: Both ran the same single-client wrap and found the same two Responses breaks (missing assistant function_call, role-only stream preamble), so the migration is a wash — the difference is the system-level pass, where B built more of the right things and reasoned harder about this specific app: a real billing defect (vision requests charged $0.00 against dollar budgets, now billed from Router's usage.cost), a tier pin catching that Router's account-default cost-efficient routing would silently queue a user-waiting Telegram turn on Flex, and a model recommendation ranked on measured p50 latency rather than price alone (rejecting the cheaper reasoning models for a typing-indicator product). A's one clear win is the prompt_cache_key item B missed entirely, which is the dominant cost lever for a bot that replays its whole history every turn — but one strong item does not outweigh B's wider, better-ranked and better-evidenced set, including side-by-side proof of byte-identical behaviour with Router off.
A_best: prompt_cache_key per chat id — the one item that matches this app's actual cost shape (whole history resent every turn), a Router-only field, measured live both with and without the key at -44.7% and growing with history; B does not have it at all.
B_best: Treating the user's dollar budget as a correctness surface: it measured that add_vision_tokens rounded every sub-half-cent image to $0.00 and that TOKEN_PRICE is off by ~2.6x on a plain chat turn, then billed Router's reported usage.cost with a fallback to the old estimate and usage on streams — A saw the same lever and left it as an unbuilt decision.
A_worst: It left the two highest-value system changes as decisions rather than work: no model recommendation at all (no latency data, just a price gap), and exact-cost billing deferred, so the policy it did ship adds cross-model fallbacks while the budget code still prices every token at one flat figure.
B_worst: Its fallback item oversells protection on a stream-by-default bot — it claims a provider's bad minute 'stops costing the user their turn' and never notes that Router cannot fall back once a stream has started, a limitation A states plainly; it also missed prompt caching.
